problem: If $Q=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ x & x\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$
worked_solution:
The matrix $Q$ is singular if and only if $det(Q)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q) & =3\cdot x-x\cdot 6 \\  & =3x-6x \\  & =-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x & =0 \\ x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $x$ is $x=0.$
